Opposition leader Maria Karina Machado says Venezuela's advance toward democracy is irreversible.
NPR's Carrie Khan reports on her first public address after her surprise
returned to the country last week.

Machado is now a direct challenge to the U.S.-backed interim president Delcie Rodriguez,

An Egyptian man has pleaded guilty to federal hate crime and other
charges for a deadly attack on demonstrators in Boulder, Colorado last year.
Prosecutors Thursday accused Mohammed Soleiman of carrying out the attack
because the demonstrators were Jewish.
The attack killed one person and injured a dozen others.
Soleiman is already serving life in prison on state charges.
Halloween is just around the corner and the cost of handing out candy isn't getting any cheaper.
NPR's Joe Hernandez reports on the rising cost of chocolate and other sweets.
According to the latest federal data, prices for candy and gum are up 7.7 percent in one year and
more than 18 percent in two years. One major culprit is chocolate. After drought and heavy
rains in places like West Africa hurt cocoa harvests in recent seasons. Global cocoa production
is rebounding, but consumer chocolate prices remain elevated and shoppers are pulling back.
That's according to data from Circana, which tracks sales in supermarkets across the U.S.
They found that people have been buying less chocolate each year for several years running,
but dollar sales are up, which means people are spending more money on chocolate,
but getting less of it. Joe Hernandez, NPR News.
